title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: I is a poset, the indexing poset of strata for the 'stratifications ordinaires de type I' defined on the next page, where X_i is the closed stratum. I is given its Alexandrov-type topology. From formula (87), \bar J = {i | ∃ j∈J, i ≤ j} is the down-closure (closure; closed sets are down-sets). \tilde J = {i | ∃ j∈J, j ≤ i} is the up-closure.

1. Bands. A subset J is a 'bande' if j,k∈J and j≤i≤k imply i∈J. This is an order-convex subset, equivalently a locally closed subset of the Alexandrov topology. The notion is symmetric under I ↦ I°, and intersections of bands are bands. The band generated by J is (84) B(J) = \bar J ∩ \tilde J = {i | ∃ j,k∈J, j≤i≤k}.

2. Domination. (85) defines J ≺ K iff J ⊂ \bar K and K ⊂ \tilde J. In words: every element of J lies below some element of K, and every element of K lies above some element of J. This is a preorder on P(I).

3. Associated equivalence. (86) J ~ K iff J ⊂ \bar K∩\tilde K = B(K) and K ⊂ B(J), iff B(J) = B(K). Each class has a unique band representative B(J). So the quotient poset P(I)/~ is the set of bands of I, ordered by domination; domination is antisymmetric on bands.

4. The band spanned by two bands. If J, K are bands with J ≺ K, then (87) I' := B(J∪K) = {i | ∃ j∈J, k∈K, j≤i≤k} = \tilde J ∩ \bar K. In I', J is closed and codense (I' ⊂ \tilde J), and K is open and dense (I' ⊂ \bar K). Conversely, if a band I' contains J as a closed codense subset and K as an open dense subset, then J and K are bands, J ≺ K, and I' = \tilde J ∩ \bar K.

Purpose: this is the combinatorial bookkeeping for unions of strata. Bands index locally closed unions of strata. A pair J ≺ K describes a locally closed piece X_{I'} decomposed as a closed part X_J and a dense open complement X_K, i.e. a recollement/gluing situation. This feeds the next page's semi-simplicial (flag) resolution and the spectral sequence (89) H^p(I, i ↦ H^q(X_i,F)) ⇒ H^*(X,F).
errors: No mathematical errors. Transitivity, reflexivity, B(J)=B(K) ⟺ J⊂B(K) & K⊂B(J) (using convexity of B(K)), and (87) all check out.
Slip in the text: 'K dense dans I', i.e. I' = \bar K' should read I' ⊂ \bar K. Grothendieck corrects this himself in the next line ('I' ⊂ \bar K ∩ \tilde J (on a même égalité!)').

ideas.what: Bands = order-convex subsets of the stratification poset, i.e. locally closed subsets of the Alexandrov topology. The generated band is B(J) = \bar J ∩ \tilde J.
ideas.modern_name: convex subposet / locally closed subset of an Alexandrov space; convex hull
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in order theory; used for poset-stratified spaces e.g. in Lurie, Higher Algebra App. A

ideas.what: Domination preorder J ≺ K iff J ⊂ ↓K and K ⊂ ↑J. Its equivalence classes are represented by convex hulls, and the quotient is the poset of bands.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Egli, Milner, Plotkin (c. 1975-76) in denotational semantics

ideas.what: For bands J ≺ K, the band generated by J∪K is \tilde J ∩ \bar K, with J closed codense and K open dense in it, and the converse. This characterizes 'closed–open' decompositions of locally closed unions of strata.
ideas.modern_name: closed/open (recollement) decomposition of a locally closed subposet
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in stratified-space theory (MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 'relation de domination' on subsets of the stratification poset is exactly the Egli–Milner order. The set of bands ordered by domination is exactly the (finite-set) Plotkin convex powerdomain construction: convex sets as canonical representatives of Egli–Milner classes. This is a theoretical-computer-science notion appearing independently, around 1981, in a geometric context (posets of strata). The link between the convex powerdomain and the combinatorics of stratifications (closed codense / open dense gluing) does not seem to be made explicitly in the literature.
missed.quote: J ≺ K ⟺déf J ⊂ \bar K, K ⊂ \tilde J (relation de domination). C'est une relation de préordre sur l'ens P(I) ... L'ens ordonné quotient est l'ens des bandes de I
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a curiosity rather than a new theorem. The poset of locally closed subposets under Egli–Milner order could serve as a natural indexing category for gluing/recollement data in exit-path and poset-stratified ∞-category frameworks. It is a minor cross-field link.

deep.surprise_reason: The material is elementary order theory on convex subsets of a poset, serving as set-up for stratification bookkeeping. The only non-obvious point is the independent appearance of the Egli–Milner/Plotkin convex-powerdomain order. That is a pleasant but minor connection.
transcription_corrections: Margin formula (84) is a definition attached to the struck passage 'La plus petite bande contenant J est ...'. It reads B(J) = \bar J ∩ \tilde J = {i∈I | ∃ j,k∈J, j≤i≤k}, '= déf B(J)'.
'On dit ... aussi, donc, que J est une bande' likely reads 'On dit aussi, dans ce cas, que J est une bande de I' (with a marginal insertion about j≤i≤k).
The insertion after 'Supposons maintenant que J et K' is 'avec J ≺ K' (soient des bandes).
'aussi [?] K est dense dans I'' should be 'enfin K est dense dans I''.
Final paragraph: 'K un ouvert dense dans I', donc J et K sont des bandes' – 'donc' is better read as 'alors'.
Page number 89 appears at bottom left.
